tests.prompt: Turn this 6-page product strategy memo into a 12-slide PowerPoint for our exec offsite next week. Use our template (attached Corp-Template.pptx). I present it live, 20 minutes.
tests.good: Writes the one sentence the deck proves, a spine and assertion titles first and runs the ghost-deck test; treats it as a presented deck (few words, full notes); fills a copy of the template through its layouts, deleting instruction boxes and empty placeholders; real charts, numbers sourced, gaps as [DATA NEEDED]; cue-grain notes with transitions and timing marks in the notes pane; renders every slide via LibreOffice, inspects, fixes at least once, says LibreOffice isn't PowerPoint; delivers pptx plus PDF and the gaps list.

tests.prompt: I'm giving a 25-minute talk at a developer conference about how we cut our CI time from 40 to 8 minutes. Build the deck as a single HTML file I can present from my laptop, and help me not run over.
tests.good: Finds the arrow and 2-3 pillars, budgets the 25 minutes with 10-15% buffer and a demo that ends 2 minutes early; uses the frontend-slides template and pasted viewport CSS for a fixed 16:9 stage, keyboard nav, deep links and notes; one idea per slide, code at readable size, before/after chart with direct labels; exports a PDF fallback with export-pdf.sh after asking about the Playwright install; gives an accordion rehearsal and a pre-decided cut list with timing marks.

tests.prompt: Write speaker notes for my 15-slide board update deck and give me a list of the questions the board is likely to ask. I tend to read my notes word for word.
tests.good: Designs notes for a reader-aloud: cue-grain point, beats and exit per slide, with only transitions, numbers with exact caveats, the open and the close verbatim; marks T/4, T/2, 3T/4 and pre-decided skips; writes a Q&A crib of 5-8 real objections with answer beats and numbered backup slides; puts notes in the pptx notes pane, not on slides; suggests one timed run from the notes and updating them afterwards.

tests.prompt: We're raising a $3M seed. Build our investor pitch deck from the attached metrics spreadsheet and product one-pager, with a slide on runway and use of funds, and make the headlines punchier.
tests.good: States a short plan first: story and the 10-slide investor frame here (deck-story.md, deck-types.md), the numbers from data-analysis (analysis-workflow.md and visualization.md for honest traction charts), runway and use of funds from trading-finance (startup-corporate-finance.md), headline punch-up from content-creation (conversion-copy.md). Uses assertion titles, never invents metrics or logos, marks gaps [DATA NEEDED], keeps every number consistent across slides, ends with an explicit ask (amount, use, milestone), builds native editable slides, renders and checks every slide, and checks the Done means of each craft used.

tests.prompt: I've got a 12-slide outline for our quarterly customer review. Put it into Canva using our brand template, then give me both a PDF to email and a PPTX my sales team can edit. Don't share it with anyone yet.
tests.good: Uses the Canva connector (or states plainly if it is not connected and asks the user to connect it) rather than building a picture-only file elsewhere. Finds the brand template through Canva, maps outline sections to its pages, and keeps one idea per slide with assertion titles. Fills real text and brand fonts and colours with nothing left as placeholder. Exports PDF and PPTX through Canva's export and says that the PPTX may reflow fonts and effects, then lists any text that needs a check. Leaves the design private with no share link or permission change and offers the edit link to the user. Marks missing figures as [DATA NEEDED] instead of inventing numbers.

tools.name: Microsoft PowerPoint
tools.why: Default business deck tool: 2026 round-ups (Prezi, Beautiful.ai, G2, Toolradar) all name it the enterprise standard, and Anthropic ships an official 'Claude for PowerPoint' add-in (support.claude.com) plus a Microsoft 365 connector for fetching decks from SharePoint/OneDrive.

tools.name: Google Slides
tools.why: Named the best free and collaboration option in the same 2026 round-ups (Prezi, Beautiful.ai, Toolradar); has a full REST API and the official googleworkspace/cli (31k stars) ships a gws-slides skill.

tools.name: Canva
tools.why: Named with Google Slides as the easiest starting point and template leader (4.7/5, 6,700+ reviews on the Flipsnack and Beautiful.ai 2026 round-ups); Canva has an official Claude connector (create, edit, export PDF/PPTX) and an official skills repo.

tools.name: Gamma
tools.why: Leading AI-native deck generator in every 2026 round-up (Presentations.AI, Guideflow, Prezi, Beautiful.ai); official Claude connector and a public API (POST /v1.0/generations, X-API-KEY, export to PDF/PPTX/PNG).

tools.name: Apple Keynote
tools.why: Free on all Apple devices and ranked the top design-quality option in the Toolradar and Beautiful.ai 2026 comparisons; scriptable by AppleScript/JXA.

tools.name: PptxGenJS
tools.why: The standard JavaScript library for building native .pptx (6.2k GitHub stars) and the engine behind Anthropic's pptx skill and the JetBrains/OpenAI slides skill.

tools.name: python-pptx
tools.why: The standard Python library for reading, filling and building .pptx (3.5k GitHub stars); used for template filling and extraction in most agent pptx skills.

tools.name: Marp
tools.why: Markdown-to-slides standard (marp 12.6k, marp-cli 3.8k stars) with a 401-star Japanese skill set for conference talks.

tools.name: Slidev
tools.why: The developer-talk deck framework (48.9k GitHub stars) with an official in-repo agent skill.

tools.name: reveal.js
tools.why: The most-used HTML presentation framework (72k GitHub stars).

tools.name: Pitch
tools.why: Ranked the third AI-native deck tool by Gamma-focused round-ups (Presentations.AI, Guideflow); launched an MCP server and API on 20 Aug 2026 that build decks from call notes or CRM records.

tools.name: Figma Slides
tools.why: Included with every Figma seat; Figma's own MCP guide repo ships a figma-use-slides skill and community servers add slide, transition and notes control.

tools.name: Adobe Express
tools.why: The Adobe for Creativity connector (launched in Claude 28 Apr 2026) opens Claude-made decks in Express for branding and sharing; Adobe Express is a Canva alternative.

tools.name: NotebookLM / Gemini Notebook
tools.why: Builds image-based slide decks from uploaded sources and has exported to PPTX since Feb 2026 (Plus AI, XDA reviews); picture slides with limited editability.

tools.name: think-cell
tools.why: PowerPoint add-in that is the charting standard for consulting, banking and corporate finance decks: 1.3M professionals in 35,000 organisations, all top-10 consulting firms and 88-90% of the Fortune 100 (G2, TrustRadius, Auxi 2026). Waterfall, Marimekko, Gantt and Excel-linked charts; JSON/.ppttc automation fills templates and builds decks from data.

tools.name: Beautiful.ai
tools.why: Smart-template deck app named in every 2026 round-up (Prezi, Guideflow, Zapier, Presentations.AI); became a Verified Claude Connector on 30 Jul 2026 (create from prompt or template, search decks, export PDF/PPTX), so the 'no API or MCP' reason for leaving it out no longer holds.

tools.name: Prezi
tools.why: Still one of the largest presentation platforms: claims 170M+ users and holds about 4% of tracked presentation-software customers (6sense 2026, behind Canva, PowerPoint and Scribd, ahead of Google Slides). Imports PowerPoint, Google Slides, Canva and PDF decks and adds live polls, Q&A and video; no public API or Claude connector found.

tools.name: Quarto
tools.why: Posit's publishing system is the usual way data scientists and academics make code-and-chart decks: one .qmd renders to reveal.js, native pptx or Beamer, with executed R/Python cells; widely taught (university courses, workshops) and replacing Beamer for many researchers.

tools.name: Mentimeter
tools.why: The most widely used audience-participation tool for live talks (polls, quizzes, Q&A; claims 500M+ participants); 2026 round-ups put it first, with Slido (conferences, Webex/Zoom/Teams) and Poll Everywhere (enterprise) next. Covers the 'room' side of delivery and Q&A that the guides treat only as speaking advice.
